correctness.rationale: The claim fixes n>=4, the ambient affine lattice Z^n, all 2n vertices, the two chart orbit types, and the normality hypothesis. Ohsugi--Hibi 1998 Theorem 1.7 gives a complete irredundant facet list after proving the fundamental independent sets are exactly the maximal rim independent sets plus the hub singleton. Every maximal independent rim set has clockwise gaps 2 or 3, giving precisely a_n sets containing a distinguished vertex and 2a_n containing exactly one endpoint of a rim edge. The two active ray matrices have respectively n+a_n and n-2+2a_n+1_{n odd} rays, and each explicitly contains a unimodular n-by-n submatrix. Thus their local toric divisor-class cokernels are torsion-free with the ranks claimed. Solving every canonical support equation over Q proves the stated n=4 and n in {4,5,7} criteria; these solutions are integral. The finite checker independently passes maximal-set enumeration, facet support and affine dimension, exact rank/determinant calculations and rational canonical solvability for n=4..11, but it is not used as an infinite proof. The only rim charts with class rank zero have n=4 and the determinant-one basis is smooth; all spoke ranks positive.

originality.rationale: A wheel-specific complete fixed-point local-divisor classification and the exceptional Gorenstein rim size n=7 were not found in the compared literature or published-record searches. The normality and facet theorem (Ohsugi--Hibi 1998), globally simple edge-polytope classification (Ohsugi--Hibi 2008), and the well-covered cycle classification are explicitly prior knowledge, not claimed as novel. The new formulas require combining facet incidences, integer divisor-class cokernels, and a two-orbit canonical-height analysis; no directly dominating wheel-local statement was identified. Novelty cannot be guaranteed by a negative search and there is residual risk of an equivalent specialty result.
residual_risks: A wheel-edge-polytope specialization equivalent to these local formulas may be buried in earlier literature not indexed by the searches.

The 1998 facet theorem plus standard toric techniques are strong structural premises; credit is limited to the explicit wheel-family specialization and surprising Gorenstein boundary, not to the underlying theorems.
The 1993 Plummer survey original full text was not inspected; its claim here is only the known combinatorial concept, not an exclusion of wheel toric geometry.

value.rationale: The exact local divisor-class groups and Cartier thresholds determine birationally relevant singular invariants of an infinite natural class of normal projective edge toric varieties. The rim Gorenstein exception at n=7, contrasted with failure at n=6 and all n>=8, is a sharp, structurally explained boundary, and the composition counts quantify growing nonfactoriality. This is not a computation of an arbitrary graph slice or a mere reproduction of a known cycle-independent-set count: the target is complete local canonical and divisor theory for both fixed-point orbits of an established graph-polytope family. No downstream conjectural applications or broad singular-locus classification are asserted.
